SURVEY UNDER PMAY-U  
 
NO. 3215.       SHRI M.V.V. SATYANARAYANA: 
       SHRI CHANDRA SEKHAR BELLANA: 
  
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any survey under PMAY -U 
to find out the demand for housing in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the year of the survey 
conducted and demand for housing in each State; 
(c) whether the Government has taken any measures to validate the 
demand and meet the targets set under PMAY-U; 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) the allocation of funds and the utilization under the scheme during 
the last three years? 
 
   ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a) to (e ): ‘Land’ and ‘Colonisation’ are State subjects. Therefore, 
schemes related to housing are implemented by State/Union 
Territory (UT) Governments in their respective regions.  However, 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) is supplementing 
the efforts of States/UTs by providing Central Assistance under 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -  Urban (PMAY -U) - 'Housing for All' 
Mission since June 25, 2015 to provide pucca house with basic 
amenities to all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country. The 
scheme is implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary -Led 
Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), In-Situ 
Slum Redevelopment (ISSR) and Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme  
...2/ 

 
-2- 
 
(CLSS). PMAY-U is a demand driven scheme and Government of 
India has not fixed any tar get for construction of houses under the 
scheme. States/ UTs have undertaken demand survey under PMAY -
U for assessing actual demand of housing for eligible beneficiaries 
and assessed a requirement of 112.24 lakh houses in the year 
2017. However, demand of housing being dynamic in nature, 
additional urban households who became eligible during 
implementation of the scheme, were also covered under PMAY-U. 
Based on the  validated demand survey and selection of 
beneficiaries and local conditions, the project proposals are 
approved by the State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee 
(SLSMC) headed by the Chief Secretary of States/UTs for further 
sanctioning of Central Assistance by Central Sanctioning and 
Monitoring Committee (CSMC).  MoHUA considers the release of 
Central Assistance based on the approval of projects by State/UT 
authorities for implementation of the project by them.  
Against the validated demand of 112.24 lakh houses, as on 
04.12.2023, a total of 118.63 lakh houses have been sanctioned by 
the Min istry based on the project proposals submitted by 
States/UTs under PMAY -U, out of which 113.42 lakh have been 
grounded and 78.27 lakh are completed/delivered to the 
beneficiaries. The total amount of Central Assistance sanctioned 
and released to States/UTs during the last three years under PMAY-
U is ₹80,712.63 crore and ₹75,148.94 crore respectively.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA

TO BE ANSWERED ON DECEMBER 21, 2023 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF GUWAHATI CITY 
 
NO. 3216.  SHRI M. BADRUDDIN AJMAL:   
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
a) whether the Government proposes to develop Guwahati city as it is 
facing severe water logjam in monsoon season as well as 
uncontrolled traffic every year; 
b) if so, the details thereof along with the funds allocated therefor; and 
c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE INTHE  
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI KAUSHAL KISHORE) 
 
(a) to (c):   As per 12
th Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban 
planning including town planning is the function of Urban Local Bodies 
(ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. Government of India 
supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ 
advisories. It provides financial and technical support to the States.  
 
The Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and 
Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines 2014 (Chapter 6: Sustainable 
Guidelines) published by the Ministry for adoption of the States also 
addresses the issues of Urban Flooding. 
 
 
…2/ - 

-2- 
 
The Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 
(AMRUT) was launched by the Central Government on June 25, 2015, for 
500 cities including Guwahati City across all States/  Union Territories 
(UTs) in the country. Under AMRUT, States/ UTs have been empowered to 
select, appraise, propose and implement projects after the approval from 
Apex Committee of Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) within 
the broad framework of AMRUT Mission.  The major thrust areas of the 
Mission are water supply, sewerage & septage management, storm water 
drainage, green spaces & parks, non- motorized urban transport and 
capacity building. Under AMRUT , funds are allocated to all States/ Union 
Territories at the beginning of the mission and not city -wise. For the 
State of Assam, under AMRUT, against the c ommitted Central assistance 
of ₹591.42 crore, ₹511.70 crore has been released for projects and 
overall, ₹600.43 crore has been released to Assam. 
AMRUT 2.0 has been launched on 1
st October 2021 covering all the 
statutory towns of the country to ensure universal coverage of water 
supply & make cities ‘water secure’. It will also ensure universal 
coverage of sewerage & septage management in 500 AMRUT cities. 
Further, Under AMRUT 2.0, rejuvenation of water bodies and wells is one 
of the main components. The admissible elements under this include 
harvesting the rainwater through storm water drains into water body  
(which is not receiving sewage/ effluent). So far, 34 water bodies 
rejuvenation projects worth ₹18.48 crore have been approved by Apex 
Committee of MoHUA under AMRUT 2.0. So far, 3 water bodies 
rejuvenation projects worth ₹1.52 crore have been taken up in Guwahati 
City under AMRUT 2.0. 
Under AMRUT 2.0, against the committed Central assistance of 
₹775 crore, a total of ₹56.65 crore have been released for projects. 
Further, ₹1.44 crore for Administrative & Office Expense (A&OE) has been 
released against the committed Central assistance of ₹25.2 crore to 
Assam.  
 
…3/ - 
 
 

 
-3- 
 
Smart Cities Mission (SCM) was launched by the Central 
Government on 25 th June 2015 to promote cities that provide core 
infrastructure and decent quality of life to their citizens, clean and 
sustainable environment through application of smart solutions. 100 
Smart Cities have been selected. The State Government has informed 
that the Guwahati Smart City Limited has taken up project of Integrated 
Traffic Management System (ITMS) in Guwahati City with 94 junctions 
with ITMS / Automatic Traffic Control System (ATCS), 10 Speed Violation 
Detection Locations (SVD) and Command Control Centre (CCC). 61 out of 
94 ITMS/  ATCS junctions and 4 out of 10 SVD locations has been 
completed. The work is going on in the remaining 33 ITMS/  ATCS and 6 
SVD locations. An amount of ₹ 78.44 crore has been given to GSCL for 
ITMS project including 5 years operation and management (O&M). 
Further, as reported by the State, Guwahati Metropolitan 
Development Authority (GMDA) has also taken up the task for preparation 
of GIS based water drainage Master Plan for Guwahati City. Under the 
Mission Flood Free Guwahati, a fund of ₹ 43.44 crore has been allocated 
by the State Government to GMDA in the year 2022-23. For GMC, the total 
budget allocated by Government of Assam for FY 2022- 23 under Mission 
flood Free is ₹47.70 crore. Additionally, works  to the tune of ₹19.81 crore 
are being implemented by Guwahati Municipal Corporation ( GMC) under 
various grants and budgetary support for construction and/ or 
upgradation of drainage systems.
